messages.content: Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.
Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.

samples.text: Floating-point numbers have a finite precision, so when two operands are added the result is rounded to the nearest representable value. Because rounding can discard low‑order bits, the error introduced by the first addition may be amplified or reduced when a third operand is added, depending on the grouping of the operations. Consequently, (a + b) + c and a + (b + c) can produce different rounded results, breaking associativity.
